ACVRL1 is a gene associated with HHT, and that mutations in this gene can be associated with HPAH, PoPAH and HPS, but that this does not mean that all patients with these conditions have ACVRL1 mutations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ACVRL-1 mutation in this family is not associated with a specific type of PH, but with a more general tendency to PH, which can manifest in different forms, depending on the underlying pathophysiological mechanism.

The main takeaway from our work is that
ACVRL1 mutations can be associated with a broad clinical spectrum in HHT and in PH.
HHT should always be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with PAH or PoPAH, even if they do not have any clinical signs or symptoms of HHT.

ACVRL1 mutations should be considered in the differential diagnosis of PH in the presence of HHT, and that the presence of a single mutation does not exclude the possibility of other genetic variants in the ACVTL1 gene or in other genes relevant in HHT.
